data.title: Statutory notice and contractual probation parameters (UK, Employment Rights Act 1996)
data.summary: The UK Employment Rights Act 1996 (c. 18) sets statutory minimum notice periods (Section 86) and governs contractual rights during initial employment. While probation periods in the UK are contractual rather than statutory, an employer may terminate an accepted unconditional employment contract before day one or during probation only by providing the agreed contractual or statutory notice pay, establishing that pre-start revocation represents an actionable contractual termination rather than costless cancellation.
data.citation: UK Employment Rights Act 1996, Section 86 (Rights of employer and employee to minimum notice).
